title: Align Stripe line items to internal usage apportionment for interleaved quota changes
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Background: We observed a class of customer reports where invoices contained Stripe line items that did not match the internal usage apportionment when customers changed quota bands mid-billing-cycle (quota upgrades/downgrades or burst credits). Root cause appears to be our export reconciler bucketing usage by hour boundaries while Stripe line item proration expects proportional apportionment across the effective time window. Scope: 1) Ensure the billing exporter computes prorated invoice amounts using the same per-second apportionment logic used by internal chargeback reports; 2) Map Stripe line_item metadata to include internal bucket ids and the original usage interval so downstream NetSuite exports are idempotent; 3) Add reconciliation assertions and end-to-end tests. Acceptance criteria: - For sampled customers with interleaved quota changes, the exported Stripe line items (amounts and metadata) must match the internal invoice builder output within 0.5% rounding tolerance. - Exports must include metadata keys: internal_bucket_id, usage_window_start, usage_window_end, apportionment_factor. - NetSuite import must consume these metadata fields and produce consistent invoice lines (validated via nightly backfill run). - Unit/integration tests and a dashboard showing before/after reconciliation diffs. Approach: - Implement a per-second apportioner that consumes usage deltas and quota-change events to compute precise fractional allocation for each billing window. - Update the billing-exporter service to attach metadata and to use the apportioner when generating Stripe line items. - Create a reconciliation job that compares Stripe-extracted lines against internal invoice model and flags mismatches. - Add staged rollout: feature-flag the exporter change, run backfill on a small cohort, validate against the reconciliation job, then enable wider rollout.
comments: 2026-02-21: Triage meeting notes: confirmed this reproduces in nightly backfill for accounts with tier changes mid-cycle. Assigned to Connor for implementation. Links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Apportionment+Investigation

2026-02-25: Spike completed. Implemented a prototype per-second apportioner and validated against sample dataset (500 accounts). Prototype reduced mean mismatch from 3.2% to 0.1%. Notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-apportionment-spike

2026-02-27: Design review feedback from PM (Ravi Patel): ensure exporter metadata uses stable keys and add a checksum to prevent duplicate NetSuite invoice lines. Action: add internal_export_checksum to metadata. See design doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/213

2026-03-01: Engineering PR opened for apportioner and exporter changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4567. Includes unit tests for boundary conditions (leap-second safe, daylight savings cutovers).

2026-03-03: QA notes: Added integration test that runs a synthetic cycle with three quota changes and asserts Stripe amounts equal internal invoice amounts after rounding. Found an edge-case when usage_rate is zero for short windows — added guard to apportioner to emit zero-line items instead of NaN.

2026-03-05: Rollout plan: enable feature-flag for 5% of production customers for one billing cycle, run reconciliation job nightly, watch 'billing.reconciler.mismatch_rate' dashboard. Dashboard URL: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/billing-apportionment
acceptance_tests: Unit tests covering per-second apportioner for: simple upgrade, downgrade, burst credit insertion, zero-usage windows.
Integration test generating a synthetic billing cycle with 3 quota transitions and asserting Stripe line amounts == internal invoice amounts (tolerance 0.5%).
Nightly reconciler run shows mismatch_rate < 0.01 for rollout cohort over one billing cycle.
NetSuite backfill import for 7-day cohort matches ledger totals and is idempotent (re-run produces no deltas).
notes: Incident learning: ENG-80712 found that naive hour-bucket proration creates off-by-one-second allocations for customers crossing DST boundaries; apportioner will normalize to UTC and store original timezone for auditing.

Trade-offs: per-second apportionment increases compute for backfills by ~2.3x; mitigated by running backfills in a larger batch worker fleet and caching previous apportionment vectors for common quota-change patterns.
Follow-ups: after rollout, consider exposing apportionment metadata in customer billing portal for transparency.
